Summary: A Roman biographer and court official whose Lives of the Caesars, written in the early 2nd century, profiles the emperors from Julius Caesar to Domitian. Key work: Lives of the Caesars.
KeyPoints: Claudius 25 says Claudius expelled Jews from Rome over disturbances instigated by 'Chrestus' — whether this names Christus or a separate agitator is debated; Nero 16 records Christians, followers of a new and mischievous superstition, punished under Nero; Together the passages confirm a Christian presence in Rome in the mid-1st century
